family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Broad family: check for latex, simple usually opposite/whorled leaves and a fused 5-lobed corolla. In local milkweeds/milkvines, go straight to the corona, gynostegium and pollinarium.
family_diagnostics.broad_family: Five stamens are associated closely with the fused corolla/stylar head; the superior gynoecium is built from two carpels.
family_diagnostics.milkweed_specialization: In Asclepiadoideae, stamens and stylar head form a gynostegium and pollen is packaged into pollinia/pollinaria.
family_diagnostics.fruit: Often one or two follicles with comose seeds on the milkweed side, but broad Apocynaceae fruit is more diverse.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: LOOK HERE FIRST: compare Amsonia's ordinary stamens and usually paired slender follicles with Asclepias' corona hoods, gynostegium and pollinaria. These milkweed structures are not universal to Apocynaceae; A. tuberosa may have clear sap. Distinguish milkvine follicles from Ipomoea capsules.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → real flower architecture → hood/horn/corona → gynostegium → pollinarium → follicle → milkvine comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Learn the broad dogbane plan first, then use real milkweed macro photographs to connect the terms corona, hood, horn, gynostegium and pollinarium to structures you can actually see.

steps.title: 1 · Broad family doorway
steps.look_for: Simple entire leaves plus latex and a fused flower; these are broad-family clues, not final proof.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents the learner from defining the whole family only by milkweed structures.

steps.title: 2 · Find the corona on a real flower
steps.image_label: Asclepias asperula flower — corona visible around the center
steps.image_alt: Close macro photograph of an Asclepias asperula flower showing the central corona
steps.look_for: The five-part crown inside the reflexed corolla. In Asclepias, the corona is built from five hoods.
steps.why_it_matters: This connects the term corona to the actual three-dimensional milkweed flower.

steps.title: 3 · Separate hood from horn
steps.image_label: Same flower — compare each hood with its narrower horn
steps.image_alt: Macro photograph of Asclepias asperula showing corona hoods and horns
steps.look_for: Each hood is the broader cup-like corona segment. The horn is the narrower projection rising from inside or near the hood.
steps.why_it_matters: Hood shape and horn presence/length are high-value milkweed identification characters.

steps.title: 4 · Look into the flower center
steps.image_alt: Cross section photograph of an Asclepias asperula flower showing the central reproductive structure
steps.look_for: The fused central reproductive column enclosed by the corona rather than ordinary separate stamens around a free stigma.
steps.why_it_matters: The gynostegium is the structural center of the specialized milkweed pollination mechanism.

steps.title: 5 · See the pollinarium
steps.image_alt: Macro photograph of an Asclepias asperula pollinarium
steps.look_for: Two pollen masses connected through the translator apparatus and central corpusculum.
steps.why_it_matters: Seeing the pollinarium makes the otherwise abstract terms pollinium, pollinarium and corpusculum much easier to remember.

steps.title: 6 · Follow flower to follicle
steps.look_for: The dry pod-like fruit that opens along one side; inside are flattened seeds that normally carry silky hairs.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit architecture links the strange flower back to the two-carpel dogbane plan.

steps.title: 7 · Compare a milkvine
steps.look_for: Twining habit, opposite cordate leaves and a specialized gynostegium/corona flower unlike a morning-glory.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that the milkweed reproductive machinery is not limited to upright Asclepias.

comparisons.title: Apocynaceae vs Convolvulaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have fused corollas and vines. Milkweed-side Apocynaceae has gynostegium/corona/pollinarium machinery and follicle fruit; morning-glories do not.

comparisons.title: Broad family vs milkweed group
comparisons.rule: Corona, gynostegium and pollinia are derived milkweed-side traits. Broad Apocynaceae is more diverse.

comparisons.title: Amsonia vs Asclepias — flower center and fruit
comparisons.rule: Amsonia has ordinary stamens and typically two slender follicles; Asclepias has corona hoods, a gynostegium and pollinaria, and usually develops one follicle per flower. Photograph the flower center and fruit together; latex is not decisive.

visual_lesson.caveat: The current local project is intentionally strongest on Asclepiadoideae; one non-Asclepiadoideae breadth card remains future visual polish.
